data.name: Sharavathi
data.gender_notes: Sharavathi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sharavathi is the name of a goddess who is believed to be the protector of rivers. She is often depicted as a beautiful and graceful goddess who brings prosperity and fertility to the land. The name Sharavathi carries the meaning “Goddess of rivers” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Kannada. Parents who choose Sharavathi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of rivers and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sharavathi represents the divine feminine energy of nurturing and abundance. She is a symbol of the creative power of nature and the transformative power of water. Her name is a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things and the importance of honoring the natural world.
data.etymology: Sharavathi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of rivers.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharavathi total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: The river Sharavathi, also known as the Saundatti River, is a tributary that flows into the Krishna River. Its source is in the Western Ghats, and it passes through the Karnataka region in southwestern India. The name Sharavathi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Sharabha', which refers to a mythological creature, a lion-headed man with the body of a serpent. This creature is believed to be an incarnation of Lord Shiva. The river is thus considered sacred, and is the site of numerous temples and pilgrimages.

The name Sharavathi is also mentioned in the works of the medieval poet-saint Allama Prabhu, who lived in the 16th century in the Karnataka region. He wrote extensively about the river and its beauty, and his poems have been a source of inspiration for generations of poets and musicians in the region.

In modern context, it is commonly referred to as the Sharavathi River, which is a major tributary in South India. The goddess Sharavathi is also worshipped in various parts of Karnataka and is believed to be the embodiment of the river.
